title: Ops & Finance Pocket Brief — Inference Deployment Tradeoffs (2026)
author: Priya Menon
summary: This pocket brief is written for platform operators and finance stakeholders evaluating LLM inference deployments. It distills the key tradeoffs across hosted, dedicated (reserved), and private (VPC/on-prem) deployment options, provides concise competitive positioning against common alternatives, a practical pricing guidance framework for pilots and scale, a one-page pitch-deck outline for operator/finance audiences, and an operator-oriented security FAQ tailored for procurement and risk teams.
audience:
- Platform operators, SREs, and capacity planners
  - Finance leads evaluating unit economics and commitment decisions
  - Security reviewers who need short, evidence-backed answers for RFPs
  - Sales engineers supporting pilot-to-production conversations
positioning:
Redwood Inference positions as a production-first inference runtime and platform that focuses on predictable economics and operational controls. For ops+finance buyers we emphasize:
  - Predictability: reserved capacity and autoscaling policies that meet throughput SLAs and predictable monthly costs.
  - Controllability: per-route quotas, model pinning, and rollout policies to mitigate regression risk.
  - Cost-levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that allow explicit cost/latency tradeoffs.
  - Risk reduction: graceful degradation via model variants and region fallbacks to maintain availability.
key-messages:
- "Predictable performance, measurable economics, and enterprise controls — without building the infra yourself."  
  - "Start with hosted for time-to-value; move to Dedicated for throughput predictability; adopt Private only when regulatory or data isolation requires it."  
  - "We expose the knobs (batching, cache, quantization) so finance can model per-token economics and ops can meet SLOs.",
messaging_bullets: "Hosted API: fastest pilot; per-token pricing; built-in telemetry for early unit-economics modeling."
"Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, committed throughput, monthly/annual contracts; ideal when variance in latency/cost is unacceptable."
"Private: customer-managed network and KMS/HSM integrations; required for regulated data and air-gapped environments."
"Optimize: automated recommendations for batching/quantization that reduce token cost 2–6x depending on workload."
"Resilience: automated fallback to smaller model variants or different region to keep the app online under stress."

pricing_guidance:
This section gives a concise framework for sizing pilot economics and extrapolating to committed spend.
1) Pilot sizing (30–90 days): choose Hosted and enable detailed telemetry.
   - Track: avg tokens/request, percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for latency, and request concurrency.
   - Fix: a conservative batch size and prefix-cache for repeated prompts to estimate effective token reductions.
2) Break-even to Dedicated (rule of thumb): when monthly token-equivalent spend >= 0.6 * monthly committed Dedicated cost (after expected batching/cache savings), evaluate Dedicated.
3) Cost knobs (how finance models savings):
   - Batching improves throughput but increases p95 latency; model tradeoffs by expected concurrency and latency SLO.
   - KV/prefix caching reduces token usage for repetitive contexts (search, chat history, templates).
   - Quantization reduces GPU cost per token with minor quality differences; run A/B on a representative eval set.
4) Contract guidance:
   - Pilot PO: Hosted with 30–90 day telemetry and a limited credit commitment line to surface usage spikes.
   - Committed: 6–12 month Dedicated with quarterly review and defined rollback/fallback (hosted) in contract.
pricing_examples:
Example 1 — Small consumer chat pilot (50k monthly active users, average 150 tokens/session):
- Hosted spend estimate: 50k * 150 = 7.5M tokens -> monthly cost = tokens * hosted_per_token_rate (use platform calculator). Expect to reduce ~20% tokens via caching.

Example 2 — Platform API with steady throughput (200 req/s peak, 300 avg tokens/req):
- Use Dedicated sizing calculator: peak throughput mapping to GPU r4/8 units, factor in 1.3x headroom for bursts, and compare committed monthly cost vs projected hosted spend.
pitch_deck_outline:
One-slide-per-topic compact deck (6 slides) targeted at Ops + Finance reviewers:
1) Title + ask: pilot scope and desired KPI (latency p95, monthly tokens, cost cap)
2) Current pain: unpredictable unit costs, tail latency, ops maintenance
3) Redwood solution: hosting modes, controls, and SLO guarantees
4) Economics: modeled pilot spend vs committed Dedicated — break-even chart and sensitivity to batching/cache
5) Risk & mitigation: fallbacks, encryption/KMS, model pinning, rollback plan
6) Next steps & PO ask: pilot timeline, ownership, success criteria
pilot_runbook:
Owner: Sales Engineering / Solutions (SE) for pilot setup. Ops lead: customer platform engineer.
Pre-launch checklist:
- Confirm data residency and KMS needs.
- Determine SLOs (p50/p95 latency, availability), define observability hooks (traces, token-level billing export).
- Provide representative prompt set and sample traffic shape (QPS, burst profile).
Launch steps (numbered):
1) Enable Hosted API access and create a sandbox key with route quotas.
2) Configure telemetry export (prometheus metrics + token billing CSV) and grant read-only access to customer team.
3) Run a 48–72 hour soak with production-like traffic at 20% scale to validate p95 and token accounting.
4) Iterate on batching and caching settings; run an eval harness on representative prompt set to validate quality.
5) Present finance model and recommend path (stay hosted, move to Dedicated, or pilot Private).
case_study_summary:
ACME FinTech (mid-market):
- Problem: variable per-session cost for chat summarization and strict data residency in EU.
- Pilot: 60-day hosted pilot with telemetry, then 12-month Dedicated commit for predictable throughput.
- Outcome: 3.6x reduction in unit cost via prefix caching + quantization; p95 latency reduced from 640ms to 220ms; finance reported forecast accuracy improved enabling a committed 12-month contract.

security_faq:
Q: How is customer data isolated in Dedicated and Private deployments?
A: Dedicated provides tenant isolation via reserved GPU pools, per-tenant namespaces, and isolated network paths. Private (VPC/on-prem) places the control plane in customer-managed network with optional air-gapped mode and KMS/HSM integration.

Q: What encryption is used in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.3 for all network transport. At-rest: AES-256 for model artifacts and metrics. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments.

Q: Who can access prompt and token logs?
A: Access is RBAC-controlled. By default only customer admins and Redwood SREs (with just-in-time access audits) can access logs. We provide export hooks so customers can ship telemetry into their SIEM.

Q: Is there a vulnerability disclosure and third-party audit program?
A: Yes. Redwood runs quarterly pen-tests with accredited firms and continuous vulnerability scanning. We provide SOC 2 Type II and can share audit artifacts under NDA.

body:
Overview
========
This brief is designed to be a single-stop reference for operator and finance stakeholders evaluating LLM inference deployments. It emphasizes measurable economics, concrete pilot steps, and concise security answers for procurement.

Sections
--------
- Positioning and one-line messages for buyer conversations
- Short competitive recap and scoring focused on cost and ops overhead
- Pricing guidance and concrete examples to model pilots
- A compact pitch-deck outline for meetings with Ops + Finance
- Pilot runbook and case-study summary
- Operator CLI examples and a focused security FAQ

Ownership & escalation
----------------------
- Primary owner: Go-to-market (Solutions Engineering) for pilot orchestration.
- Escalation: Engineering SRE for performance incidents; Security for compliance evidence requests.

Success criteria for pilots (example)
------------------------------------
- Observability: token-level billing export in place and validated within first 7 days.
- Economics: modeled per-session cost within 15% of projected value after caching/quantization tuning.
- Latency: p95 meets the agreed SLO for at least 95% of test windows during a 7-day soak.
- Security: KMS/certificate configuration verified and pen-test checklist passed for Private pilots.

Appendices
---------
Appendix A — Representative telemetry fields to collect:
- request_id, timestamp, route, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, GPU_util_pct, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, error_rate

Appendix B — Suggested eval metrics for finance/ops alignment:
- quality delta at quantization profile levels (none, 8-bit, 4-bit)
- effective tokens saved by prefix caching (baseline tokens vs cached tokens)
- throughput uplift from batching vs p95 latency impact
